hints: Focus on the carbon atom that is directly bonded to the OH group, not just on the presence of OH.
Count how many other carbon atoms are joined to that C-OH carbon: one means primary, two means secondary, three means tertiary.
Test each column in a row with that count, and look for the row where the counts go 1, then 2, then 3 in order.
walkthrough:
**Recall the classification rule**

Alcohols are classified by the environment of the C-OH carbon. It is all about connections.

Primary: $\text{C-OH}$ bonded to 1 other C. Secondary: $\text{C-OH}$ bonded to 2 other Cs. Tertiary: $\text{C-OH}$ bonded to 3 other Cs.

**Check the simple reference row**

Look at row D first because the structures are simplest. Primary: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. The $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ carbon is joined to 1 C, so primary.

Secondary: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. The $\text{CH(OH)}$ carbon is joined to 2 Cs, so secondary.

**Complete the check and conclude**

Tertiary in row D: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$. The $\text{C(OH)}$ carbon is joined to 3 $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so tertiary.

That gives primary, secondary, tertiary in order, so this row is correct. The other rows all contain diols or triols where every $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is still primary.

options.A: Primary column is correct as propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. But the secondary column is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, propane-1,2-diol, which contains one primary OH and one secondary OH. The tertiary column is $\text{CH}_2\text{OHCH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, propane-1,2,3-triol, which has only primary and secondary OH groups and no tertiary C-OH carbon.
options.B: Primary column is actually correct as a primary alcohol, since the OH is on a $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group. However the labels are swapped afterwards. The secondary column shows $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, where the C-OH is bonded to 3 carbons, so it is tertiary. The tertiary column shows a $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group bonded to only one other carbon, so it is primary.
options.C: All three molecules are built only from $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups. Each C-OH carbon is bonded to only one other carbon, so every OH shown is primary. There is no secondary $\text{CH(OH)}$ and no tertiary $\text{C(OH)}$ in this row, a common trap when extra $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ branches are mistaken for increased substitution.
options.D: This row is perfect in order. Primary: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, C-OH joined to 1 C. Secondary: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, propan-2-ol, C-OH joined to 2 Cs. Tertiary: $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, C-OH joined to 3 Cs.
